title: G5: Relative dependency graph and SCC decomposition processor

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
Define the relative dependency graph $\mathrm{DG}_{\mathrm{rel}}(R,S)$: nodes are pairs of $\mathrm{DP}_{\mathrm{rel}}(R,S)$, with an edge $P\to Q$ iff some relative chain has $P$ immediately followed by $Q$ (i.e. $t_P^\#\sigma\to_{R\cup S}^{*}s_Q^\#\sigma$).

**Must prove:**
- **Soundness of SCC decomposition:** $(\mathcal P,R,S)$ is finite iff every SCC, treated as its own relative DP problem, is finite. (Every infinite chain eventually stays in one SCC — uses König's lemma / finiteness of $\mathcal P$.)
- **Computable estimation:** give a decidable over-approximation of edges (relative analog of $\mathrm{CAP}/\mathrm{REN}$) that accounts for $\to_S$-connectivity, and prove it over-approximates the true graph. The presence of nonterminating $S$ means reachability $t^\#\sigma\to_{R\cup S}^*s^\#\sigma$ is more permissive; ensure the estimation remains sound.
